biography.background:
Bert est un Humain Engineer "Roboticist". La technologie et la robotique sont ses passe-temps. Il est capable de bricoler des drones en quelques secondes et de les exploiter au maximum durant ou hors des combats. Il est également accompagné de "S.M.A.S.H", son robot compagnon !

Comment jouer Bert ?

  • Vous êtes humain, le Stress ça vous connaît, vous pouvez l'absorber mieux que d'autres.

  • Vos connaissance de Forgeborne vous permettent d'avoir des avantages sur les réparations, la fabrication ou le bidouillage de n'importe quel appareil.

  • Déployez des drones et des appareils qui vous serviront à vous et à vos alliés avec @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart-scifi-content.character-options.cWCfF37m7YPuRW2W]{Field Devices} !

  • Vous êtes un spécialiste des sciences et de la tech, si quelque chose ne se passe pas comme prévu, utilisez @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart-scifi-content.character-options.139uKV0SfomfSmUJ]{Ingenuity} pour changer les événements.

  • La connaissance c'est le pouvoir, si le jet d'un allié rate, dites lui comment faire en lui donnant un avantage sur son reroll avec @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart-scifi-content.character-options.6mUfKFyCbxLGh5BE]{Live and learn}.

  • Votre @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart-scifi-content.character-options.s6J3Xqecns5hUJPq]{Companion Robot} se chagera d'attaquer les ennemis au corps à corps pendant que vous restez à distance en sécurité.

  • Utilisez votre Scanner Tactique pour détecter les formes de vie autour de vous, avant de tomber dans une embuscade !

What’s the most important thing you’ve ever built… or destroyed?

Do you solve problems for the joy of the work, the challenge, the paycheck, or something else?

What piece of tech have you been trying to design for years but can’t get quite right?

system.description: When you or an ally fails a roll, you can spend 3 Hope to reroll with advantage.

Once per session, you may spend a Hope and explain with some technical and incomprehensible words why something that just happened isn't quite possible. Then do one of the following:

  • Avoid marking a Hit Point, Stress or Armor Slot.

  • Add or substract 2 from any roll (include adversaries).

After the first time you use this feature during a session and once per scene, you can use Ingenuity by giving the GM a Fear instead of spending a Hope.

system.description: When you fail a roll that utilized one of your Experiences, you can mark a Stress to reroll.
You have Advantage on the Work on a Project downtime move if it requires you to make a roll to advance a countdown. You can also take the Work on a Project downtime move during a short rest.

Your companion acts during your turn. You are in permanent communication with it. It can:

  • Move (it cannot fly but can move in Zero G).

  • Attack in melee (using the same benefits you have as well as your Proficiency).

  • Interact with its environment.

  • Activate one of your @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart-scifi-content.character-options.cmQ1erqGqemNvB7U]{Field Devices} if in Melee range of it.

  • Talk.

Your companion has 3 Stress markers starts with an Evasion of 10. Everytime your companion would take any amount of damage, it marks a Stress. When it marks its last Stress, it deactivates and remains unavailable until the start of your next long rest. When you choose a downtime move that clears a Stress on yourself, your companion clears an equal number of Stress.

Attack and damage.

Your companion starts with a d6 damage dice and Melee range. Make a Spellcast roll to attack.

Training.

When your character levels up, choose one of these options for you companion:

  • [0/3] Resilient: your companion gains an additional Stress slot.

  • [0/1] Armored: when your companion takes damage, you can mark one of your Armor Slots instead of a Stress.

  • [0/3] Hydraulics: increase the damage dice by one step (d6 to d8, d8 to d10, etc.)

  • [0/1] Not My Master: when you mark your last HP, your companion rushes to save you. It takes 1d6 Stress point instead of you taking a HP.

  • [0/3] Aware: your companion gains +1 to its Evasion.

You can spend a Hope to set your companion in and out of Turret mode.

While in this mode, it cannot move but can deploy a range weapon dealing d8+8 physical damage (still using your Proficiency, bonuses and Spellcast roll) at Far range.
Your companion can fly, hover, ignore difficult terrain.
Humans are most easily recognized by their dexterous hands, rounded ears, and bodies built for endurance.

Being part of a forgeborne community means you were raised in massive industrial complexes, orbital foundries, or bustling shipyards where construction and repair never truly stop. Your people solve problems with ingenuity, tools, and perseverance rather than brute force.

Forgeborne are often diligent, inventive, patient, resourceful, steadfast, and meticulous.
Play the Roboticist if you want a permanent robotic companion.

Mark a Stress to boost the equipment of an ally within Close range or your own equipment. Apply one of these effects to your target:

  • Add 1d6 damage to the next successful attack made by the target with a primary weapon.

  • Grant +2 Evasion to the target until they are hit by an attack.

Recon Drone: Mark a Stress to deploy a small floating bot that you can move anywhere within Very Far Range. While this ability is active, you can see through the bot as though you’re in its position. You can transition between using your own senses and seeing through the bot freely. If the bot takes damage or moves out of range, the ability ends.

Medical Drone: Make a Spellcast Roll (13) and target a creature other than yourself within Melee range. On a success, mark a Stress to clear 1 Hit Point or 1 Stress on the target. You can't heal the same target again until your next long rest.

Movement Detector: You can place a number of movement detectors up to your spellcasting trait. Each detector is able to sense movement in a Very Close range and send you a notification when it does.
